instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.
public_summary:
Scene 003: exactly one real-robot episode ran; `finish_episode` was called to close it, after 65 rounds.

Observation: The cup was picked up, but after release it landed on its side on the table rather than remaining suspended. Final success requires confirmation by the on-site operator.

The final retreat movement was rejected because the authorization lease was insufficient and was not executed. The robot arm remains enabled; on-site operator inspection and takeover are required.

manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Hang the cup on the rack.

Task description: Lift the handled cup and hook its handle over one of the bars of the wooden cup rack at the center of the table, letting the rack support the cup.

Success criteria: The cup has been picked up, the cup-rack support bar passes through the cup handle hole and supports the handle, and the cup is hanging. Merely touching the handle to the bar while the gripper still supports the cup does not count as hanging it successfully.

## Execution tips

- For the white cup in front of the current gripper, consider gripping a rim-wall section away from the handle, one finger inside and one outside. Set the opening for wall thickness and pad clearance, leaving room to thread the handle onto the rod.
- Before closing, confirm the fingers are actually inside and outside the cup wall with sufficient pad contact, rather than gripping only the top rim. If the gripper obscures the view, adjust the observation position slightly to avoid mistaking image overlap for surrounding the wall.
- If the cup body needs turning, adjust it in the open space outside the rack, watching the sweep of the base and gripper to reduce contact with adjacent rods or posts.
- Choose a rod with a clearly visible free end and ample surrounding clearance. Align its tip inside the cup handle opening and fine-tune the handle orientation to the rod direction. If the handle edge presses against the tip, retreat and correct rather than continuing to push and risk tipping the rack.
- Before releasing, lower slightly so the inside upper edge of the cup handle bears on the support rod. Confirm that the handle is not merely balanced on the rod tip, then release gradually to avoid loss of support or slipping.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start this authorized physical-robot episode only once with the specified parameters, operate from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.

I have read the manual for this run; only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the approach pose to grasp the cup wall near the rim and away from the handle, then will check grasp stability after lifting.

The handle faces the cup rack, and there is room to approach the cup. Next I will reduce movement increments gradually and close only after confirming that one finger is inside and one outside the cup wall.
The gripper is still above the cup and has not closed. I am lowering in steps of no more than 1 cm and checking the cup wall and pad positions after each one.
The gripper is approaching the cup opening, and the cup remains stable on the table. I need to descend slightly more so the pads grasp the cup wall rather than touching only the rim edge.
Both views show one finger inside the cup and the other outside its wall. I will lower slightly to increase contact area, then close and make a short test lift.

During a short test lift, the cup rose with the gripper and its measured opening remained around 5.3 mm with no visible slipping. I will continue raising it and look from outside the rack for a rod that can enter the handle.

The cup is off the table and remains held. Two rods on the rack's left overlap in the image. I am using small movements to determine their depth relation, avoiding mistaking image overlap for handle-to-tip alignment.
The cup remains securely grasped. I am turning it outside the rack so the handle opening faces more toward the lower rod on the left, then will approach in small steps from the rod tip.

A recoverable joint-limit rejection occurred during rotation; returned feedback showed partial arm motion. I adjusted pitch using the measured pose and executed successfully, continuing small-step alignment within this episode.

The handle now faces the selected lower rod, with clearance remaining between cup and rack. Next I will continue height and lateral adjustments, releasing only after confirming the rod enters the handle and starts bearing its weight.
The cup handle and rod tip still have not contacted. I am correcting relative height and depth, continuing approach moves no greater than 1 cm and watching for rack displacement.

The cup rack has not visibly moved, and the gripper opening remains stable. After the handle approaches the bar tip, I will move slowly along the bar and check whether it actually passes through the hole.

The bar tip is near the outer edge of the cup handle, but insertion is not yet confirmed. I will reduce the step size to about 5 mm and observe the contact point; if the handle presses against the bar tip, I will back away and correct it.

The rod tip is near the lower edge of the cup handle opening, but insertion depth is unclear. I am adjusting the height and keeping the gripper closed rather than treating image overlap as a confirmed hang.
The rod tip is within the projected area of the cup handle opening, and the rack remains stable. I will lower slightly to check the support relationship before deciding whether to gradually release.

The image shows the lower support rod passing through the upper part of the cup handle opening, and the stand has not moved after the cup was lowered. I will gradually release the gripper and check whether the rod independently supports the cup.
As the gripper opened gradually, the cup lowered only slightly and remains on the post. Next I will move the pads away from the cup wall and observe whether it continues to hang.

After full release, the cup fell onto the table and lay on its side, showing that it was not effectively hooked and cannot count as success. The cup rack does not appear to have tipped. I will first move the gripper away, inspect the cup opening and handle again, and assess a feasible recovery grasp within this episode.

On reinspection, the cup opening faces away and the handle lies close to the table. The current image cannot confirm a safe recovery grasp. I will move the gripper away from the rack and end this episode. My observation-based judgment is that the cup was lifted but not securely hung.
The retreat was rejected by the safety mechanism: the operator authorization lease could no longer cover the entire action. The tool returned `done=true` and the action was not executed. I will send no more motion commands and immediately call finish_episode. Arm enablement is unchanged; the on-site operator must inspect and take over.
